item.title: Chris Pappas Could Make History in New Hampshire’s Senate Race

item.title: How Title IX Became a Political Tool
item.description: After a Cornell student’s lawsuit alleging the school failed her when she reported sexual assault, there’s a new focus on Title IX, the federal law barring sex discrimination in federally funded education. Our Washington correspondent Michael C. Bender traces how interpretations of the law shifted between the Obama and Trump administrations.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender, Gilad Thaler, Nikolay Nikolov, Rafaela Balster and Pierre Kattar

item.title: Cornell Case Highlights Shifting Federal Title IX Enforcement
item.description: From Barack Obama to Donald Trump, ideology has infused the interpretation of the federal law banning sex discrimination on college campuses.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: An allegation of a gang rape at Cornell in 2024 has put renewed attention on the 54-year-old law known as Title IX.
